% amsmath, with a \bmatrix of the document's that takes an argument. Its
% \bmatrix{...} in the rows of a numbered align is no macro pair of
% amsmath's: each row keeps its number, and its \label names that number.
% Inline too.
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{amsmath}
\renewcommand{\bmatrix}[1]{\left[\begin{matrix}#1\end{matrix}\right]}
\begin{document}
\begin{align}
x &= \bmatrix{1 \\ 2} \label{own-a} \\
y &= 3 \label{own-b}
\end{align}
Rows \eqref{own-a} and \eqref{own-b}. Inline, $M = \bmatrix{a & b \\ c & d}$.
\end{document}
